items.summary: At Adobe MAX, the companies announced an expanded partnership bringing Adobe's creative and productivity tools into everyday Google apps like Drive and Gmail. The deal also brings Google AI models into Adobe products. Features include PDF editing from search results, image connectors in Gemini, enterprise collaboration through a CX agent, and explorations with DeepMind for Photoshop edits.
items.title: Adobe and Google Expand Partnership at Adobe MAX

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder, was sued on Nov 9 in a proposed class action accusing the company of defrauding shareholders by concealing his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. The shares closed 4.3% lower that day after a probe was announced, shrinking market capitalisation by around US$190 billion. Analysts say fundamentals remain strong as AI demand grows and customers stay locked into Nvidia’s CUDA platform; the company guided revenue of about US$108 billion for its third quarter of fiscal 2027, roughly 12% higher than the prior quarter, with results due Nov 17. Concerns also point to possible policy-driven slowdowns in AI spending and data centre construction as Democrats gain congressional control; Goldman Sachs estimates 45% of planned US capacity faces restrictions, while about 75% of new 2027 capacity is already under construction at around 24GW. The main risk discussed is whether Huang steps down amid the investigation.
items.title: Nvidia faces legal and leadership uncertainty over Jensen Huang affair

items.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, an AI solution in preview designed to unify fragmented clinical, operational, and administrative systems into coordinated action. The platform integrates skills and data connectors with third-party electronic health records, billing platforms, clinical guidelines, and Medicare datasets to orchestrate workflows like medical records synthesis and prior authorization review under guardrails and human oversight. It is available alongside launch partners HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health. Context notes clinicians lose nearly 28 hours each week to paperwork.
items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare

items.summary: A regulatory filing showed on Nov 10 that Anthropic’s initial public offering could raise up to US$64.4 billion (S$82 billion), with a valuation of up to US$1.02 trillion based on Reuters calculations, per the company and investors’ plan to sell shares at between US$70 and US$78 each. The deal would total up to US$90.4 billion including private placement from cornerstone backers such as Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia and Microsoft. Anthropic posted a narrower third-quarter net loss amid revenue rising 47% to US$16.96 billion. Its filing warned of competitive and safety risks while citing nearly US$900 billion in computing commitments.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for US$1 Trillion IPO as Wall Street Tests AI Optimism

items.summary: Keith Porcaro, on Nov 10, 2026, asks whether the United States could seize control of Anthropic well below its $1. 4 trillion target IPO valuation. He notes that under the Fifth Amendment's Takings Clause, seizing private property requires just compensation but not a premium; in his example, buying all common stock costs only $2 per share. The key complication is governance: unlike Meta or Alphabet, Anthropic concentrates control through a Class T trust and a Founder LLC holding 50. 1% of voting power while surrendering nearly all economic value to public shareholders. Because the controlling shares carry little economic worth, compensation could fall far short of $1. 4 trillion. Porcaro flags that such a move would be legally novel, likely trigger lawsuits and engineer departures, but might occur in an emergency or if Anthropic fell out of government favor.
items.title: A Discounted Path for a Government Seizure of Anthropic

items.summary: Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, introduced Gemini for healthcare on January 27, 2026, as a purpose-built industry solution extending the universal Gemini agent. He noted that general AI models alone cannot address fragmented healthcare data and cited clinicians spending nearly 28 hours a week reconciling information across disconnected systems. The offering provides four core components: reusable skills for clinical and administrative tasks; connectors to EHRs like Epic, Oracle Health, InterSystems FHIR Server, Verato, and Keragon Healthcare Integrations (400+ applications); eligibility and claims tools including Optum Coordination of Benefits (currently in limited release) and TriZetto Provider Solutions; terminology resources such as ICD-10 Codes and RxNorm Drug Vocabulary; CMS Coverage integration with Medicare rules; evidence guidelines from Optum EvidenceVue and BMJ Digital Health; plus enterprise productivity integrations like Salesforce, Suki, UiPath, Synthpop Careflow, Alteryx, Sana from Workday, ServiceNow, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Cyera Dataport. Built to support HIPAA compliance with governance, audit logging, verifiable citations, and open model choice between frontier and fast models, the platform is available in preview in the U.S., developed alongside clinical and health plan leaders including HCA Healthcare, Northwell Health, Optum Insight, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, and American Society of Clinical Oncology.
items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare in preview

items.summary: Anthropic could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists on New York's Nasdaq this month, offering shares between $70 and $78 each to raise up to $64bn. The figure is below the $2tn some backers predicted in summer, though revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn over six months while pre-tax losses rose to $80.7bn amid a volatile market for AI firms.
items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut Prices Below Backer Hopes

items.summary: Robin Kirman, a psychoanalyst and novelist, argues that OpenAI's August launch of Teen Mode—an automatic version of ChatGPT for users under 18—reflects an industry admission of responsibility for harms to young people. While the feature adds guardrails against harmful content and introduces Study Mode as a Socratic learning tool, Kirman contends it fails to address a deeper harm: by constantly guiding teens through their thinking, Teen Mode may deprive them of the unassisted struggle needed to form an independent sense of self. She links this concern to research connecting rising teen anxiety and suicidal ideation with technology displacing unsupervised time. The piece closes with crisis support information for the US, UK/Ireland, and Australia.
items.title: OpenAI's Teen Mode May Undermine Teens' Developing Sense of Self

items.summary: Anthropic updated its IPO filing Tuesday, offering 825 million Class A shares at an estimated price range of $70 to $78 per share. The sale could raise between $57.75 billion and $64.35 billion, with net proceeds expected between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion. At the top of the range, Anthropic would be worth a hefty $1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from its May fundraise valuation but below its earlier $2 trillion target.
items.title: Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range and $1.4 Trillion Valuation

items.summary: Kirt McMaster, co-founder of the defunct Cyanogen Android venture, has unveiled Kora Systems’ new Linux-based desktop operating system aimed at users who depend heavily on artificial intelligence in daily work. Announced Tuesday, the software integrates AI models and autonomous agents across applications while retaining context between tasks. It is expected to launch free-to-use in 2027 for Intel-, AMD- and Qualcomm Snapdragon-powered PCs. McMaster estimates that 45 million to 50 million people currently account for much of AI usage, a market he expects to exceed 200 million users by 2033. Revenue will come through subscriptions bundling access to AI models and agentic services.
items.title: Cyanogen Co-Founder Launches AI-Focused Windows Rival

items.summary: The Philippines' IT and business process management (IT-BPM) sector continued expanding in 2025, defying expectations that artificial intelligence would displace its workforce. According to the IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines, the industry employed about 1.9 million people and generated US$40 billion in revenues in 2025, with the contact centre segment adding roughly 60,000 workers to reach 1.68 million. The reported figures were described as early indicators rather than causal estimates of AI's impact.
items.title: Philippine outsourcing industry grows despite AI fears

items.summary: Rohan Sharma responds to a Nov 6 article on Singapore authorities urging limits on AI agent autonomy, arguing that users must also know where an agent's access begins. He cites guidance from the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore and two other agencies showing how linking accounts—such as Meta's Muse connecting Facebook, Instagram or Threads automatically—reveals the problem.
items.title: Singapore urges AI providers to disclose agents' account access

items.summary: The Google team says Gemini 4 Argon acts as a simulation engine that generates thousands of varied practice runs from real camera scenes and builds realistic digital twins, helping the robot generalize faster to new scenes and objects when combined with demonstrations. They describe it as an important milestone toward physical AGI, advancing dexterity, reliability, and safety for robots working alongside people.
items.title: Google DeepMind unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 powered by Gemini 4 Argon

items.summary: A Tech Policy Press analysis argues Cambodia's scam crackdown has not stopped the industry, which continues to spread globally. Moses Ngeth reviewed thousands of Telegram recruitment ads and found operations relocating to Myanmar, Vietnam, Timor-Leste, Pakistan, Georgia and Nigeria. HRC analysts note experienced managers now list their skills openly, signaling a mature illicit labor market. Mark Taylor says crackdowns target forced workers while sparing bosses. In October 2026, Vietnamese police charged 88 foreigners in romance scams targeting six countries, estimating $50 billion dong misappropriated. Ngo Minh Hieu estimates starting a scam operation costs under $4,000. Chiang warns networks and experience persist regardless of location.
items.title: Cambodia's Scam Crackdown Fails as Industry Spreads Globally

items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers introduced AlphaProof Code, a framework that used AI agents with human oversight to formally verify the compiled code of Signal's cryptographic protocol. The work claims this is the first time an AI has verified such a widely deployed protocol at implementation depth, and that it completed in four weeks versus years historically.
items.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Code

items.summary: The film industry faces a dystopian prospect as AI generates stories and recreates screen icons, but its immediate impact already reaches behind-the-scenes jobs. Hollywood figures like James Cameron sit on an AI board; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered animation; Christopher Nolan called the idea of replacement “nonsense” yet conceded useful imaging tools arise. The clearest target is the storyboard artist: Martin Scorsese partnered with an AI firm in June for storyboarding his next film, and even Bong Joon Ho likens shooting without them to standing in Grand Central Terminal wearing only underwear. Artists stress that boards are collaborative art, not just drawings; Ferdinando Cocco notes a return to analogue practice and sees communication forcing creative expansion. Alex Clark predicts greater appreciation for films with a human touch as AI grows.
items.title: Film Artists Warn AI Threatens Storyboard Craft

items.summary: Kirt McMaster, CEO and cofounder of a startup building the Linux-based desktop operating system Kora, says it targets “the AI native, not mass market.” Announced Tuesday, Kora aims to integrate context across multiple AI tools at the system level rather than siloing them into apps or browser tabs. It is scheduled to launch sometime in 2027 and runs on Qualcomm Snapdragon PCs next year as well as x86-64 hardware. The company’s team of under 100 people optimizes Kora for desktops with at least 64 gigabytes of RAM, which it says doubles the capacity of Googlebook OS.
items.title: Kirt McMaster Positions AI-Focused Kora OS for Creators

items.summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade approved new regional price ceilings for ground-mounted and floating solar projects, effective Nov. 5, 2026. Ground-mounted maximums range from VND 1,104.32/kWh in the south to VND 1,591.02/kWh in the north; floating rates run higher, up to VND 1,939.74/kWh. Storage-equipped projects qualify for still-higher ceilings. The new figures exceed the 2025 framework across all regions and categories and set maximums rather than guaranteed tariffs, leaving purchase prices open to negotiation with buyers including Vietnam Electricity (EVN). Solar capacity passed 19 GW by end of 2025.
items.title: Vietnam Raises Solar Price Ceilings for 2026

items.summary:
Delegates from roughly 200 countries opened COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, the first UN climate summit since scientists signaled that a key warming limit has been missed. The UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report found best-case warming would peak at 1.7 to 1.8 degrees Celsius around mid-century, requiring emissions to fall 45 percent below 2025 levels by 2035 — a cut not on track. Reporter Bob Berwyn argues the overshoot era is an invoice for past underinvestment rather than grounds to skip negotiations, where countries set emission cuts, adaptation and financing each year. Adaptation finance falls short: even tripling it would raise only $85 billion to $120 billion annually against developing nations' estimated need of $305 billion. Reporter Keerti Gopal noted the loss and damage fund's first round covers less than 1 percent of Nepal's losses, underscoring the shortfall Berwyn says must not be spent on less.

visual null
items.title: Climate Delegates Reject Overshoot as Excuse for Inaction

items.summary: A study published on 24 September in IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity outlines CERN's work manufacturing next-generation magnets for the Large Hadron Collider. The current collider uses niobium-titanium coils reaching about 8.3 tesla, roughly 166,000 times Earth's magnetic field. Scientists are developing niobium-tin (Nb₃Sn) coils yielding just under 12 T using a wind-and-react process. Magnet engineer Susana Izquierdo Bermúdez leads a team of about 60 people who produced 250 coils, with 25 failing quality control tests. The High-Luminosity LHC aims for between 140 and 200 particle collisions per experiment after 2030, requiring these compact magnets to observe rare phenomena.
items.title: CERN Engineers Next-Generation Magnets for High-Luminosity LHC

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Chinese financing documents assigned servers worth 432 million yuan ($64.8 million) to Moonshot, though Bloomberg could not establish whether U.S. approval existed under export rules barring the chips from China without express consent. Moonshot denied involvement in the arrangements and said it had no business relationship with server owner Lingmeixin or ownership of the equipment. Nvidia and Super Micro also disclaimed any customer ties; a White House official separately asserted that Moonshot accessed Blackwell chips via Thailand, while CNBC reported possible European neocloud rentals.
items.title: Moonshot AI Rented Restricted Nvidia Chips Inside China

items.summary: TSMC plans an investment of up to $1 billion across AI developers Anthropic and OpenAI, its board approving $500 million each for shares at IPO price. The move signals confidence in long-term chip demand amid rising AI spending concerns. TSMC remains the world's largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to firms like Nvidia, reporting six consecutive record-profit quarters with 2026 revenue growth of about 44 per cent.
items.title: TSMC Commits Up To $1 Billion Across Anthropic And OpenAI

items.summary: Amazon's Ring launched a robotics business with two autonomous security products on Tuesday, expanding beyond its home-security lineup. Both devices use the AI Pilot system to map spaces and navigate obstacles. The Ring Rover patrols businesses autonomously, while the Ring Drone flies preset routes or responds to alarms. Amazon will ship the Ring Rover Cam on December 16 at $999.99 in the US, and the Ring Drone Cam on January 27 at $249.99.
items.title: Amazon's Ring launches autonomous flying camera and security robot

items.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang faces growing scrutiny over alleged Chinese espionage ties and personal relationships, prompting a 5% stock drop on Monday. Yale expert Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates his chances of staying are 50-50, while Bernstein cites heavy reliance on him as a risk but keeps its Outperform rating with a $400 target.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Leadership Uncertainty Over Jensen Huang

items.summary: Meta announced it will expand artificial intelligence-based age detection across its platforms, including Instagram, Facebook and Threads, starting November 9. If the system believes a user is under 18 despite claiming an adult birthdate, Teen Account safety rules may apply globally. Meta faces legal challenges over minors' wellbeing on social media.
items.title: Meta to use AI age detection on Instagram teen accounts worldwide

items.summary: Major Wall Street firms hold hundreds of billions in Nvidia exposure yet appear unconcerned about the trouble surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon told CNBC that key-man worries are overblown, arguing no ecosystem depends on one person and Nvidia will remain a major American company. The bank is part of a consortium committing $500 billion to fund Nvidia's AI expansion.
items.title: Wall Street Stays Calm Amid Jensen Huang Scandal Concerns

items.summary: Anthropic is set to launch its initial public offering late next week, according to The Wall Street Journal, signaling confidence in demand for the AI sector despite a recent market selloff and concerns about Nvidia. Separately, TSMC reported a 60% revenue increase year over year, reflecting sustained hardware demand. Investors remain cautious about an impending AI bubble and rising opposition to data centers amid midterm elections.
items.title: Anthropic Moves Forward With IPO Amid AI Market Uncertainty

items.summary: In a speech at the Bank of England Watchers Conference on November 10, 2026, Federal Reserve Board member Christopher J. Waller laid out his view that further monetary tightening is warranted despite a stable labor market. He noted strong U.S. economic growth and an unemployment rate near its long-term level, but flagged inflation well above the FOMC's 2 percent goal. While he supported holding rates at the most recent meeting because markets had already priced in hikes, Waller said that if October CPI data arrive high—around 0.3 percent or more—he would back a 50 basis point increase at the December meeting; otherwise he leans toward a 25 basis point hike. He warned that low hiring and firing may signal reduced labor market dynamism with implications for productivity, while elevated core goods prices and energy pressures could sustain inflation into 2027.
items.title: Fed Governor Waller Urges December Rate Hike Amid High Inflation

items.summary: US prices rose 0.4% in October, below September's 0.6%, yet still above the 0.3% analysts had expected. The rise was driven by increases in housing, food and energy costs, though energy price rises slowed to 0.7% from 5.2%. Because inflation came in higher than forecast, analysts say it raises the chance of an interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December meeting; governor Christopher Waller had already signalled a lean toward raising rates even if October figures were slower. The Bureau of Labor Statistics measured the change through the consumer price index and did not publish a 12-month figure for October after failing to collect data in time, while noting inflation was 3.7% over the year to September.
items.title: US October Inflation Beats Expectations, Raising Fed Rate Hopes

items.summary: The UK government launched a leak inquiry into how Bloomberg reported bank tax details hours before the budget, with Chancellor John Healey to face questions. Separately, higher-than-expected October US inflation pushed stocks lower and raised odds of a December rate hike.
items.title: UK launches leak probe as US inflation jolts Wall Street

items.summary: Gasoline dipped below $4 a gallon Tuesday, per AAA, after falling 38 cents in the last month to $3.98 nationally. Yet consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the Labor Department, exceeding forecasts, with housing costs driving much of it. Rising diesel and freight costs add pressure as heating oil climbs amid cold weather.
items.title: Gas Prices Fall as Inflation Stays High

items.summary: US inflation rose 0. 4% from September to October, a slight cooldown as gas costs fell during the month, though it edged above expectations. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release its usual year-over-year figure because data was not collected in October 2025 amid the government shutdown. Energy prices remained elevated, and inflation has stayed above an annualized 3% since late February. AAA reported gas averaging $4. 41 at month start to $4. 22 by end of October. Fed chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank remains focused on easing price increases while keeping expectations anchored.
items.title: US Inflation Cooled in October as Gas Prices Dipped

items.summary: The average transaction cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. reached a record high of $51,109, according to a report from Kelley Blue Book, part of Cox Automotive. That figure is roughly $500 above the prior December 2025 record and up about 2.1% over the past year — below inflation, Erin Keating noted. The transaction cost includes sticker price, add-ons, minus incentives, but excludes auto-loan interest. Rising production costs from tariffs on steel, aluminum and Canadian goods; higher chip and copper prices; and a shift toward larger vehicles all push prices up. Meanwhile, used cars average close to $27,000, 6% higher than last year.
items.title: U.S. New Car Costs Hit Record $51,109 Average

items.summary: The da Vinci 5 surgical system is making its debut at the China International Import Expo (CIIE), featuring advanced robotic technology designed to help surgeons perform complex procedures with greater precision and control. CGTN took a closer look at this cutting-edge medical equipment, describing it as an example of innovative healthcare machinery showcased at the event.
items.title: Da Vinci 5 Surgical System Makes CIIE Debut With Advanced Robotic Technology

items.summary: On The Hub, Wang Guan speaks with George Katrougalos, Independent Expert of the United Nations Human Rights Council and former Foreign Minister of Greece. An editor's note frames the world as undergoing profound transformation. Their conversation explores whether the international system can become more democratic and equitable, what role China and Europe may play in a multipolar order rising from the Global South, European political integration, UN reform, and China's Global Governance Initiative.
items.title: Interview on Building a More Equitable Global Order

items.summary: An editorial by Zhang Xuan, director of the Energy Strategy and Policy Research Institute at China Southern Power Grid (CSG), explains why Beijing is investing heavily in a new-type power grid. According to the National Development and Reform Commission, investment over the 2026-2030 five-year plan is expected to exceed 5 trillion yuan (about $749.27 billion). The author argues that conventional grids cannot absorb rising wind and solar output, which by end of September 2026 reached 2.01 billion kW against a total capacity of 4.13 billion kW. Rather than simply expanding transmission, the plan aims to transform grid functions through backbone, distribution and microgrid systems supporting reliability, green absorption and industrial needs. The article reflects the author's opinions and not necessarily those of CGTN.
items.title: China Plans Trillion-Yuan Transformation of Its Power Grid

items.summary: Greta Thunberg opened Cop31 in Antalya warning that climate change threatens everything and everyone, urging action to protect people rather than sacrifice the global majority for a few. The summit coincides with Turkey announcing two new oilfields and other nations expanding fossil fuel output despite transition pledges.
items.title: Thunberg Warns as Cop31 Opens in Turkey Amid Fossil Fuel Debate

items.summary: Defense secretary Pete Hegseth called Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment a ‘political spectacle’ and personal ego-driven attack during his Pentagon press conference. The House is poised to vote on whether to refer the resolution for investigation or table it, with possible floor action by Wednesday.
items.title: Hegseth dismisses impeachment as political spectacle

items.summary: French police made arrests after searching three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris and Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, on 13 and 14 October 2026. The Metropolitan Police confirmed a number of arrests following interviews with several victims. Searches were conducted alongside British investigators as part of an investigation into alleged abuse by Mohamed Al Fayed.
items.title: French Police Arrests in Al Fayed Abuse Probe

items.summary: The Associated Press reports that many defectors view Kim Jong Un's daughter, reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, as the likely next leader of North Korea. Since late 2022 she has made dozens of public appearances with her father at weapons tests and military parades; state media calls her 'most beloved' child, and eight of the 11 defectors interviewed by the AP shared that view. Doubts remain rooted in her gender: only one of 17 department directors for the ruling Workers' Party is a woman. Observers nonetheless expect Kim Jong Un to designate a successor who will face little resistance at home, as past successions suggest passive acceptance.
items.title: Defectors See North Korea's Kim Jong Un Daughter as Likely Heir

items.summary: The documentary "The Sea We Call Home" is presented through director's notes that describe its approach rather than report measurable findings. Rather than advancing a predetermined argument, the film centers five personal stories about people who have lived by the South China Sea for generations: an island dweller, fishermen following ancestral routes, reef divers, those adapting to shifting fishing grounds, and residents of Tanmen waiting for boats. The notes explain that disputes appear only as context while restraint guided its telling.
items.title: Director's Notes on The Sea We Call Home

items.summary: CGTN reporters are returning to the people and islands they filmed more than a decade ago, marking their comeback after thirteen years. The series, titled 'The Sea We Call Home,' will premiere on November 11 and explores familiar faces, old memories, and new beginnings that reveal how much has changed in lives and on these home islands.
items.title: CGTN Reporters Return After Thirteen Years for New Documentary

items.summary: Indonesia's vice president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, offered to resign during a Tuesday meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, according to officials. The talks lasted over two hours and followed mounting questions about his academic credentials after the Supreme Court ruled they did not meet election requirements. It was unclear whether Prabowo accepted the offer.
items.title: Indonesian Vice President Offers Resignation Over Eligibility Questions

items.summary: Researchers at the University of Pretoria’s Institute for Sustainable Malaria Control argue that scientific progress against malaria is not turning into effective action. They identify three obstacles: prediction versus preparedness, evidence versus implementation, and awareness versus behaviour. Although sub-Saharan Africa accounts for around 95% of global cases, early-warning systems such as Ethiopia’s in Bahir Dar have shown detection can inform planning. A study involving more than 7,500 people found that while most recognised symptoms, bed net use remained low due to cost and access. The World Health Organization reported in April 2025 that more than 40% of planned insecticide-treated net campaigns were delayed or at risk. Closing the gap requires strengthening health systems, improving community access, and coordinating across borders, particularly in southern Africa where malaria crosses national lines.
items.title: Three Barriers Blocking Malaria Science Into Action in Africa

items.summary: A PhD student in economics and behavioural researcher Sophia Seelos tracked two decades of crop cycles and protests in Kenya, combining satellite-measured plant greenness with the Armed Conflict Location Events Dataset (ACLED) for 2000 to 2019. They found that approximately 7% of all protests over this period related to agrarian conditions, and that unrest increased two to three months after harvest, peaking around sowing as households faced financial stress during the lean season. The authors suggest governments, donors and social protection programmes could anticipate these periods using local agricultural calendars.
items.title: Kenyan Agrarian Protests Follow a Seasonal Pattern

items.summary: The European Union's ENISA agency says artificial intelligence is reshaping cybersecurity, shrinking the time between a vulnerability being discovered and weaponised to near zero while acting as a force multiplier for both attackers and defenders. In its latest report it notes that 57.3% of cyber incidents in 2025 were ideologically driven by geopolitical events such as Russia's war against Ukraine and Middle East conflicts, with most having limited impact; another 29.3% were financially motivated, ransomware remaining the most impactful type on businesses. A cited 2025 NIS Investment study found that 45% of surveyed organisations struggled to find cybersecurity-skilled staff. ENISA urges member states to expand activities and amplify EU programmes in the field.
items.title: ENISA Warns AI Is Speeding Up and Industrialising Cyberattacks

items.summary: A newborn Kalkanovatos ray took its first swim minutes after hatching at an aquarium near the Sani hotel on Greece's Kassandra peninsula, then was released into the Thermaic Gulf. The release is part of the five-year-old Thermaikos Biodiversity Project, which coordinates with the Lamna Institute in Valencia and iSea to rescue rays accidentally caught in fishing nets whose eggs may be expelled under stress. Two pups have already hatched and been returned this year.
items.title: Newborn Kalkanovatos Ray Released After Hatching in Greece Aquarium

items.summary: As the United States, China and Russia prepare to meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19, Japan is watching for changes in Washington's approach to the Indo-Pacific. Tokyo fears that President Donald Trump may seek a diplomatic quick win after his midterm-election losses, one that could overlook its allies' interests. Experts say he might treat Taiwan as leverage or ignore rare-earth export restrictions China placed on Japan. Analysts also warn about US outreach toward Russia and North Korea. Rather than rely solely on the alliance, Tokyo has diversified security partnerships with European Union states, NATO, Australia and others while reaffirming its commitment to preserving regional stability.
items.title: Japan watches Trump's foreign policy before APEC

items.summary: The Information reported that Nvidia's Jensen Huang affair with a Chinese businesswoman allegedly facilitated at least $7.5 billion worth of the company's chips reaching Chinese firms, citing two people who know her. Alice Huang and relatives built companies across China and Singapore; Shanghai Century Litong gained priority chip access by October 2023. When restricted orders stalled, she used ties to secure about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China. Nvidia did not comment immediately.
items.title: Report ties Nvidia chip shipments in China to Jensen Huang affair

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's long-running CEO and co-founder since 1993, is under an independent board investigation into allegations he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving a woman suspected of working for China. The company says it has no current reason to believe sensitive material was exposed. Analysts are sceptical the controversy will force Huang out, while President Trump defended him ahead of Nvidia's November 17 earnings report.
items.title: Nvidia founder faces investigation amid AI dominance concerns

items.summary: The Supreme Court asked WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries for measures to prevent digital arrest scams, directing them to share proposals with the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre. The court reiterated that banks must compensate victims when their failure of due diligence contributes to fraud. It also directed RBI to submit a list of authorised financial institutions before the next hearing.
items.title: Supreme Court Demands Fraud Prevention Plan From WhatsApp and Banks

items.summary: The Supreme Court of India, headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, directed tech companies such as WhatsApp and other intermediaries to submit proposals for preventing digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. The order follows Indians losing ₹800 crore to cybercrimes so far in 2026. During the hearing on 29 October, senior advocate Kapil Sibal said WhatsApp had taken action against about 9,400 accounts and was developing software to flag suspicious activity. The bench also directed financial institutions to compensate victims when fraud results from a bank's failure to exercise due diligence. Intermediaries must report measures both to the Court and to the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C). PTI reported the order, which arose in a suo motu case on forged-document arrests listed for further consideration on 23 November.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders WhatsApp and Intermediaries on Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: The US-based Rosen Law Firm filed a class-action lawsuit in California federal court accusing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his company of failing to disclose information about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed. The suit alleges the undisclosed affair raised national security concerns that misled shareholders and inflated Nvidia's share price.
items.title: Rosen Law Sues Nvidia and Jensen Huang Over Chinese Spy Affair Allegations

items.summary: A report suggests Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, 63, may become vulnerable if Democrats take control of Congress in January. The concerns follow allegations that his partner Alice Huang is suspected by US intelligence agencies of being a Chinese asset, and questions about her ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which reportedly bought Nvidia AI chips. Corporate governance experts cited by the New York Post warn the controversy could trigger scrutiny over corporate accountability and national security. A lawyer familiar with the company told the paper: "There's no way this guy survives after the Dems start holding hearings." Trump has defended Huang as an honourable figure.
items.title: Nvidia CEO could face trouble under Democrats rule

items.summary: Anthropic is targeting a $1 trillion valuation in what could become one of the biggest IPOs in history, planning to raise nearly $90 billion through a public offering and private placement. The company reported an $81 billion run-rate revenue as of October 31, 2026. Its board members have shown interest in purchasing shares at the offering price.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $1 Trillion IPO Valuation Amid AI Expansion

items.summary: Bhai Dooj, also called Bhau Beej, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The article offers a collection of more than 25 Happy Bhai Dooj wishes, messages, greetings and WhatsApp status updates to share with siblings. It describes how sisters apply tilak while brothers receive gifts as ways of expressing affection and gratitude.
items.title: Happy Bhai Dooj wishes and WhatsApp status updates for brothers

items.summary: On Monday, Kolkata police commissioner Ajay Nand ordered the suspension of inspector Ekhlaque Ahmed for allegedly making derogatory remarks against the West Bengal government on a social media platform. The order placed Ahmed under suspension pending an inquiry into whether his conduct was prejudicial to public service and transferred him to the 1st Battalion of the Kolkata armed police.
items.title: Kolkata police officer suspended for alleged WhatsApp remark against Bengal govt, CM Adhikari

items.title: Supreme Court Orders Intermediaries and Banks on Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries to submit action plans against digital arrest scams, related cybercrimes, and impersonation of law enforcement agencies. The bench, headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued the direction in a suo motu case heard over several months. WhatsApp reportedly banned 9,400 accounts linked to such scams after an investigation. Proposals must also be sent to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The matter will next be heard on November 23, 2026.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders WhatsApp Action Plan Against Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: Bollywood actress Kangana Ranaut shared a religious meme mocking the NVIDIA controversy over CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, who is reportedly linked to Chinese espionage. She added that researching her film Emergency led her to allege foreign influence killed several members of the Gandhi family, reviving criticism of the political dynasty.
items.title: Kangana Ranaut mocks NVIDIA spy row with meme and Gandhi claim

items.summary: An unknown gunman shot dead Mohammad Sharif, an accused linked to the 2008 CRPF camp attack, at a group centre in Rampur on Tuesday. Bystanders allege he was fired upon multiple times; police have launched a manhunt for the shooter. The incident follows similar killings by unidentified gunmen of Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives earlier this year.
items.title: Unknown Gunman Kills CRPF Camp Attack Accused in Rampur
